preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns r and, for every a,b with 0 <= a <= b < len(nums), if nums[a..b] is continuous (meaning for all i,j with a <= i <= b and a <= j <= b, |nums[i] - nums[j]| <= 2), then r >= (b-a+1) * (b-a+2) / 2.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let n = len(nums). For each a with 0 <= a < n, let e(a) be the largest b with a <= b < n such that nums[a..b] is continuous (where nums[a..b] is continuous iff for all i,j with a <= i <= b and a <= j <= b, |nums[i] - nums[j]| <= 2). Such e(a) exists because b = a always works. The function returns r, and for every a,b with 0 <= a <= b < n, nums[a..b] is continuous if and only if b <= e(a). Equivalently, for each a the continuous subarrays starting at a are exactly nums[a..b] for a <= b <= e(a). Moreover, r = sum over a = 0 to n-1 of (e(a) - a + 1).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; nums is nondecreasing, i.e. for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1, nums[i] <= nums[i+1].

statement: Let n = len(nums). For each b with 0 <= b < n, let s(b) be the smallest a with 0 <= a <= b such that nums[a..b] is continuous (where nums[a..b] is continuous iff for all i,j with a <= i <= b and a <= j <= b, |nums[i] - nums[j]| <= 2). Such s(b) exists because a = b always works. Then for every a,b with 0 <= a <= b < n, nums[a..b] is continuous if and only if a >= s(b), and the function returns r with r = sum over b = 0 to n-1 of (b - s(b) + 1).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.
